speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: asked the Minister for Communications and Information (a) what are the tangible outcomes of the grants provided under the SMEs Go Digital programme since it was introduced; (b) how has it helped SMEs in terms of value adding and improvements in productivity; and (c) whether there will be further improvements to enhance the effectiveness of the grants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Earlier this year, the Infocomm Media Development Authority, or IMDA, which administers the SMEs Go Digital programme, worked with the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) to evaluate the scheme's impact.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: For instance, firms which adopted the Productivity Solutions Grant, or PSG, saw overall increases in Value Add Per Worker and revenue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: The Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) regularly reviews the SMEs Go Digital programme to ensure that it remains relevant to firms' needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: In 2021, we launched the CTO-as-a-Service, which is a one-stop platform that helps SMEs tap on the available support under the SMEs Go Digital programme more effectively.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: Besides a wide suite of digital solutions and subsidised digital consultancy for SMEs, the platform also brings together initiatives by SkillsFuture Singapore, the Cyber Security Agency, the Personal Data Protection Commission and other Government agencies to help firms improve their capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: MCI has also progressively refreshed our Industry Digital Plans, or IDPs, which help to curate the support provided under the SMEs Go Digital programme to meet specific needs in over 20 sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: This year, we will be refreshing the Retail and Security IDPs and launching the Legal IDP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: These will feature a refreshed digital solution roadmap as well as updated roadmaps for digital skills, cybersecurity and data protection measures to better support our SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: That said, we know that the digital landscape is fast evolving, and our work to help SMEs reap the benefits of digitalisation will have to continue.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Minister for Communications and Information)
text: As shared at MCI's Committee of Supply debate earlier this year, we will be developing the Digital Enterprise Blueprint over the coming months to identify new challenges faced by SMEs and outline the Government's approach to help SMEs thrive in our growing digital economy.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I read the feature articles on the impact evaluation for the SMEs Go Digital Programme and it was recently included in the Economic Survey Report.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: It was mentioned that whenever there are tailored solutions, the outcome tends to be better for the SMEs.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: So, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State whether in the Digital Enterprise Blueprint that MCI is working on now, are there going to be more emphasis on tailored solutions.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: My second supplementary question is: it is good that we have all these improvements and outcomes, better value-add to the workers and so on.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
text: I want to ask whether the good outcomes are also because of the COVID-19 period where enterprises tend to want to adopt digital means because of the restrictions and whether this momentum will continue now that we are post-COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: On the first question about the benefits being greater for the SMEs when they use tailored solutions, I will make a couple of observations.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is really because of the state of our digitalisation and transformation efforts in our economy across industries and companies.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: There is no sector in Singapore that is not touched by digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: However, having said that, the low-hanging fruits or the easy benefits of using digital technology or solutions are largely reaped.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: It is how firms can better use digital technologies by going deeper, transforming their business operations – transforming not just their customer-facing operations, but also how they work with their vendors, partners and supply chains in the broader ecosystem they are in.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Therefore, we have to look at sector by sector.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The SMEs in the manufacturing sector will have very different needs from the SMEs in the retail, hospitality or legal profession.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: That is the reason why we work very hard with the trade associations and partners to develop Industry Digital Plans so that the technology roadmaps, the digital skills recommendations and solutions that are available to those SMEs would be specific to their needs.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These will be some of the focus areas for the Digital Enterprise Blueprint over the coming months.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The second point that Mr Liang asked was about whether COVID-19 has helped to accelerate the pace of digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Anecdotally, we hear many businesses say that, thankfully, because of their early investment in digital technologies and solutions, they were able to operate even during the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: They had their business continuity plans in place.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Their workers and employees could continue to work remotely offsite.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: They could continue to service their customers and clients remotely – even customers and clients who are not based in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Anecdotally, we do hear feedback from our companies, including SMEs saying that they had benefited from early investments in digital technologies.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In my conversations with many of the towkays at SMEs, business owners and management of companies, they also indicate to me they are not resting on their laurels.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Many of the conversations have shifted at the management level, at the board level, from seeing digitalisation and technology as a cost centre to one of investment in capabilities, investment for greater competitiveness and better productivity for their employees.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I am very glad these conversations have shifted partly, perhaps, due to COVID-19, but they reinforce the point that we must not lose these gains.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We should continue to hasten our digital transformation because, as a system, I believe our ecosystem in Singapore, our business environment, can enable us to be thriving competitive economy that can allow us to create new opportunities for companies and all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is great to hear that companies are benefiting from CTO-as-a-Service since 2021.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Just want to ask the Senior Minister of State since 2021, has there been any learnings from the service and any tweaks, particularly impact, in terms of scaling up and impacting more companies and raising awareness.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The second supplementary question is, it is also good to note that the Ministry is tracking the productivity gains of SMEs Go Digital.

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But does the Ministry also track the mental wellness gains or impacts on the workers in these firms as well?

speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Because I believe that productivity and wellness go hand in hand.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The intent was to give SMEs the confidence and convenience to go digital.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: SMEs, through this platform, can better access their own individual company's digital readiness through a set of checklists, through a set of assessment, maturity assessments, so that they can better choose a set of solutions to work for their needs, tailored to different sectors.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: If they need to go further, there is a consultancy that they can tap on to get advice on how they can proceed on their own digital transformation journey and a set of resources that are available to them on the platform.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Since the launch, we are very glad to see many more companies coming on board and benefiting from these solutions.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: In fact, I am heartened to see smaller mom-and-pop shops coming on board, not just the mid-sized companies, but smaller companies who realise and understand the benefits of digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Through our process of engaging these companies and through the feedback from our consultants who are part of the CTO-as-a-Service consultancy, we have identified areas where we can enhance our programme.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: This was announced earlier this year as part of MCI's Committee of Supply debate.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: A few things, for example – I would not go through the long list – the Member can refer to our speeches as part of the Committee of Supply debate – but some areas were how we enhanced the platform to incorporate vendor reviews from other user SMEs so that we can improve the quality of the vendors in the platform.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Because many SMEs tell us they understand the benefits of digitalisation, but are concerned with cybersecurity attacks and personal data breaches.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: So, we convened a set of consultants appointed by CSA and PDPA to advise these SMEs.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: These are just some examples how we enhanced the programme and I encourage the Member to look at our speeches in March this year for greater details.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: The second question by Mr Edward Chia was around whether we track the mental wellness of the employees.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I must say not at this point in that specific set of questions that he asked.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: Hopefully, that also correlates to the well-being of the employee.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: We do not just look at workers hired and the value-added per worker, which is indicative of productivity gains but also, importantly, salary increments, wage increments.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: I do believe that these are important contributors to a person's mental well-being and emotional well-being.

speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
text: But this is the feedback we will take into consideration.
